correctness.rationale: Every word-period corresponds to a border. Distinct full internal zero-gap lengths prohibit any proper border containing two ones. A zero-only border yields exactly the circular gap list (g1,...,g[m-1],a+e-ell) for ell from zero through min(a,e), so the closing gap ranges over [max(a,e),a+e]. Reflection symmetry of circular gaps requires one equality with three markers, the central equality with four, and is impossible from five onward. A one-marker border exists exactly when a<=last internal gap and e<=first internal gap, gives distinct circular gaps of one fewer marker and therefore contributes only for three markers; at most two markers are always symmetric. A direct standalone Python checker exhaustively tested 19530 eligible words through length 18, 600 seeded further words, and 150 independent conjugacy tests; those tests corroborate, not prove, the universal result.

evidence: The 2024 symmetric-period characterization is a general equivalence, but the new border restriction, the two possible border shapes, the one-marker border inequalities, and the dihedral zero-gap obstruction are needed to derive the exact test.
Earlier analysis of products of two palindromes (2015) handles the special period equal to word length; it does not cover the three-marker words requiring a smaller period.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A result about being a palindrome pair is strictly weaker as a decision procedure: there are non-palindrome-pair words that still have a symmetric shorter period. The disjoint specializations to Sturmian and automatic languages do not subsume all words satisfying arbitrary pairwise different gap lengths. There is thus no established prior implication with identical strength.

value.rationale: A complete infinite-family classification of palindromic periodicity on naturally gap-distinct binary words; the exact sharp maximum of four markers and arithmetic border thresholds expose a real structural boundary. The criterion applies to arbitrary ordering of unequal gaps and distinguishes genuinely shorter symmetric periods from words that themselves are products of two palindromes. It eliminates exponential search through periods/splits for succinct run-length data; not an arbitrary finite table or routine notational restatement.
